$comment: THE PARTITION for the scripts/ reorganisation (workstream W9, phase P0).
WHY IT EXISTS. Driver contract section 5d records a collision that is invisible
until both halves land: W7 relocates 23 JS and TS files out of .ci so that tree
becomes single-language, and their natural home is scripts/, which is exactly
where W9 installs a set-equality layout gate. Whichever lands second turns the
other red. The agreed ordering is that W9 publishes this file FIRST, with a
declared home for every relocated family, and W7 then relocates INTO those homes.
WHY IT IS PATTERNS AND NOT A FILE LIST, which is the whole design. An enumeration
of the 218 files tracked under scripts/ today is stale on the next commit, and
peers are writing into this tree right now: three files under scripts/ were
modified within sixty seconds of this file being drafted. A rule set classifies a
file that does not exist yet, an enumeration cannot, and driver contract section 6
already forbids hand-typed counts for exactly this reason.
HOW A FILE ADDED AFTER THIS FILE WAS WRITTEN IS CLASSIFIED. Three tiers, and the
third is the one that matters:
1. Rules are tried IN ORDER and the FIRST match wins. Order is semantics here
exactly as it is in .ci/scripts/ci/scope-map.cjs, so a rule inserted in the
middle changes the answer for everything below it. Any mover states where
its rule sits.
2. A file matching a rule belongs in that rule's `home`. When `home` equals the
directory the file is already in, the rule is a STAYS declaration and the
`stays` field carries the references that break if it moves anyway.
3. A file matching NO rule is `unclassified`, and unclassified is RED, never
quietly fine. The layout gate names the file and refuses. That asymmetry is
the point: forgetting to declare a new family is loud, while a wrong
declaration is at least a decision somebody made. A partition whose default
is 'accept' cannot tell a new family from a typo.
generatedBy: hand-written; scripts/lib/domains.ts is the reader and the classifier

rules.why: The ci-runner is the manifest's own home. manifest.ts carries 139 gate-path references and 409 id: literals, and driver contract section 3 gives it exactly one writer, the root driver's merge queue. Moving the directory would put a rename inside the one file the whole programme serialises on.

W2 is sole owner (driver contract section 3). The binder also identifies itself by comparing process.argv[1] against its own import.meta.url at gate-bind.ts:1521, and its inScope test requires a path under .ci/scripts, scripts or .ci/rediacc_ci.

Control tests, invoked by name from package.json (for example check:ci-locale-currency and check:ci-embed-asset-freshness each append a scripts/__tests__/*.control.ts leg). Their paths are inside the package.json command strings the root driver owns.

Baselines, seeds and content. Driver contract section 5d asked for the content files to be moved out to data/; the seven NIS2 directive .txt files (2.16 MB) and their manifests are ALREADY here, so that obligation is satisfied and must not be undone. scripts/data/enumeration-vacuity-baseline.json is the file P2 must not disturb: it is an object with a note and a single sorted `unguarded` array whose entries are gate paths, and a rename reads to that gate as growth rather than as a rename.

Shared modules imported by relative path from roughly 30 gates. scripts/lib/gate-header.ts and scripts/lib/policy-paths.ts are single-writer files (driver contract section 3). This was the destination of the scripts/utils/ merge, which COMPLETED on 2026-09-06: console.ts, crc32.ts and translation-diff.ts landed here, scripts/utils/ is gone, its 24 importers were re-pointed and the dead allowDefaultProject glob eslint.config/typescript.js:138 was dropped in the same change. There is no rule for scripts/utils/** any more because no such path can exist.

The live VM drill batteries. This prefix is load-bearing in five places and two of them fail SILENTLY GREEN rather than red, which is why the directory is pinned rather than merely inconvenient to move.
breaksIfMoved: .ci/scripts/ci/scope-map.cjs:233 matchPrefix('scripts/drills/') with full: 'harness'. A missed prefix downgrades CI scope, so a drill edit would classify reduced and skip the whole VM matrix.
.ci/scripts/ci/greenlight.cjs:421 lists 'scripts/drills' in the cache-key closure. A missed prefix reuses a stale green.
.ci/rediacc_ci/quality/scope_scripts_reachability.py:443 uses scripts/drills/lib.sh as its positive control.
.ci/rediacc_ci/tests/gates/test_gate_scope_engine.py golden expectation, and the anti-vacuity harness fixture subject.

rules.why: The one file under scripts/dev that is NOT operator-only, and the reason scripts/dev survives W9 P2's move. .ci/legacy/run-legacy.sh:793 dispatches it as `./run.sh worktree` and .ci/rediacc_ci/tests/gates/test_gate_worktree_devbox_teardown.py:31 lifts remove_worktree's body as its SUT, so it is gate-tested and scripts/ops (`why`: nothing but a human runs these) would be a false description of it. This rule sits BEFORE operator-bash because first match wins; without it the file would match no rule at all and the layout gate reports UNCLASSIFIED.
notes: Moving this file is a change to .ci/legacy/run-legacy.sh and to the teardown gate test in the same commit, not a git mv. W9 P2 declined to make it, because run-legacy.sh was owned by a concurrent writer and the exception was already declared.

rules.why: Node helpers that a workflow step calls, born at their final home rather than under .ci/scripts/ci, which the incoming-ci-helpers rule drains. scripts/ci/write-shard-receipt.cjs is the first.
notes: scripts/ci/write-shard-receipt.cjs is named by scripts/gate-bind.ts (RECEIPT_WRITER) and by the quality-code shard receipt step in ci-quality.yml; scope-map.cjs pins it to full CI under the scripts-shard-receipt rule.

rules.why: Operator-only tools: a human runs them by hand and no workflow, npm key, run.sh verb or gate invokes them. Surveyed 2026-09-06, ten are unambiguously operator-only (apply-cf-redirect-rules.sh, backup-d1.sh, bws-map-refresh.py, deploy-bench.sh, .ci/rediacc_ci/ops/derive_shadow_pass_list.py, linode-cluster-validation.sh, r2-oneshot-scrub.sh, reset-bench.sh, backup-cutover-preflight.sh, .ci/rediacc_ci/ops/build_server.py) and four more are operator-run with a CI-side reader or test.
rules.blockedOn: CLEARED 2026-09-20: the move landed. Fourteen files arrived from scripts/dev/, scripts/docker/ and the scripts/ root as git renames, after W8 P1a-P6 and W0.1 had made their edits at the old path and were all ticked. scripts/docker no longer exists; scripts/dev keeps worktree.sh alone under the devbox-bash rule above.

scripts/dev/worktree.sh is NOT operator-only and did NOT move; it has its own rule, devbox-bash, immediately above this one.
breaksIfMoved: REPOINTED 2026-09-20, all six, in the change that moved the files. The list is kept because it names the shape of the damage a FUTURE move would do, not because any entry is still outstanding.

.ci/rediacc_ci/quality/silent_failure_patterns.py:80 carries scripts/ops, as the retired bash twin did at its own line 73. A missing directory makes find return nothing and the gate reports success over half its corpus. SILENTLY GREEN.

.ci/scripts/security/shfmt.sh:121 loops over `scripts/dev scripts/ops` guarded by [[ -d ]], as does its twin's OPTIONAL_SCOPES at .ci/rediacc_ci/security/shfmt.py:92, so a scope that stops existing silently stops being format-checked. SILENTLY GREEN. A third sweep of the same shape lives at .ci/legacy/run-legacy.sh:488.
scripts/gates/check-worker-secret-names.ts:66 parses scripts/ops/deploy-bench.sh with a floor of 20.
.ci/scripts/quality/check_bws_map.py:100 reads scripts/ops/secret-rename.py as its rename oracle, built as ROOT / "scripts" / "ops" / ... so a path-literal grep cannot see it.

test-bws-map.sh:40 and :58 and test-vacuity-floors.sh:115 name paths under scripts/ops (a third, .ci/scripts/test/gates/test-scrub-sentinel-empty.sh:40 and :56, was retired in W7 P5 census batch A8), and three Python gate tests build the same paths out of pathlib parts.

Dockerfile:12 and :32 named scripts/ops/build-server.sh in comments only, which was also the only thing keeping it out of check-dead-bash's findings. The twin was ported to .ci/rediacc_ci/ops/build_server.py and deleted on 2026-09-22 under ruling 7; those same two comments now name the module, and they are what admits it through check-dead-python's mentioned route, an operator tool having no wiring to be reached by.

rules.why: Two shell scripts that are pinned by NAME somewhere outside scripts/.
breaksIfMoved: scripts/eslint-heap.sh: three package.json keys (check:lint, fix:lint, lint) plus .ci/scripts/quality/check_lint_scope_coverage.py:99 ESLINT_RUNNER = "eslint-heap.sh", and it is a registered gate leaf at scripts/ci-runner/manifest.ts:90.

scripts/pre-commit-check.sh: .claude/hooks/pre-bash/block-protected-files.sh:30 hardcodes the literal path in its PROTECTED regex. It has zero npm keys and its real wiring lives in the operator's untracked local settings, per .dead-bash-allowlist:56.

rules.why: Discovered by tsc at this path and by eslint's projectService walking up from scripts/**/*.ts. Under the driver contract's own .json predicate, a config a tool discovers at a fixed path and offers no configurable alternative for stays where the tool looks for it.

The TypeScript gate bodies, 125 of them. THE P2 MOVE IS DONE: they left scripts/ for scripts/gates/ on 2026-09-09, so this is now a STAYS declaration, and the references that break if they move again are the ones the move had to rewrite: the npm script commands in package.json, the leaves entries in scripts/ci-runner/manifest.ts and the generated scripts/ci-runner/gates.lock.json, the knip root entry glob, and 219 further files across .ci/, .claude/, scripts/ and packages/.
notes: scripts/gate-bind.ts's inScope test accepts any path under `scripts`, so scripts/gates/ stays visible to the binder.
Every moved file sits one directory deeper, so its own root derivation gained one `..`; 259 lines across the 125 files were rewritten for that and for the relative import specifiers.

rules.why: Files that WRITE artefacts rather than assert about them. Keeping them mixed in with 117 check-*.ts is the reason `scripts/` reads as a single undifferentiated pile. THE HOME ITSELF IS THE FIRST PATTERN, added 2026-09-09: the rule declared `scripts/gen` as a destination and matched only files still sitting OUTSIDE it, so the first file to actually arrive there -- scripts/gen/gen-manifest.ts -- went UNCLASSIFIED and red. A rule that reds at the moment the move it asks for succeeds is the finish-line trap; the same line will be needed for scripts/ops when the operator-script leg lands.
rules.blockedOn: CLEARED 2026-09-20: the leg is complete. scripts/gen-docs.ts and scripts/gen-gates-lock.ts were the last two subjects, held back while W11 and W2 edited them concurrently; both workstreams have handed over and both files now sit at scripts/gen/. scripts/lib/doc-providers.ts and scripts/lib/doc-regions.ts are libraries under the `libraries` rule, not subjects of this one.

rules.why: Eight .cjs helpers W7 relocates so .ci becomes single-language: greenlight, label-guide-comment, report-nightly-status, scope-engine, scope-map, skip-plan-reconcile, validate-pr, watchdog-monitor. (A ninth, autopilot-guide-comment, was removed completely along with the rest of the Autopilot subsystem; see agent/plans/PLAN-remove-autopilot.md.)
notes: scope-map.cjs is a single-writer file (driver contract section 3) and rule ORDER inside it is semantics. It moves last of the eight, and whoever moves it states where its rules sit.
greenlight.cjs:421-423 lists 'scripts/drills', 'run.sh' and '.ci/legacy' in its own cache-key closure; relocating the file does not change those strings but relocating anything they name does.

rules.why: The seven-module streaming SEA injector (cli, common, elf, index, macho, pe, verify). It replaced postject because postject could not inject a blob this large, see issue #525, so it is load-bearing for every release build.
compress-cast-idle.mjs and process-cast-markers.mjs, the tutorial cast post-processors.

The ESLint-JS-API driver behind check_lint_rule_liveness.py. Its Python entry point STAYS at .ci/scripts/quality/, because four places name that path: package.json, scripts/ci-runner/manifest.ts, .github/workflows/ci-quality.yml, and the anti-vacuity registry in .ci/rediacc_ci/tests/gates/test_gate_gate_anti_vacuity.py. Driver contract section 5d's rule applies: the ENTRY POINT lives where the binder can see it, the logic may live anywhere.
notes: Do NOT add the .mjs to manifest.ts's `leaves` list. check-ci-parity.ts:488-495 derives `leaves` from the package.json command's shell structure and reports the extra entry as a hygiene finding, and scope-map.cjs:134 already forces the full harness scope on any .ci edit.

rules.why: The single .ts file under .ci/scripts. scripts/tsconfig.json already includes ../.ci/scripts/**/*.ts, so this file is type-checked today and stays type-checked after the move by the ./**/*.ts include.

heartbeat.mjs is a tutorial FIXTURE application, not tooling. It is the twenty-third file in W7's raw JS-and-TS count under .ci and it must not be relocated with the other twenty-two: it is content the tutorial harness runs, and .ci becoming single-language does not mean a fixture app stops being JavaScript.

openQuestions: Driver contract section 5d says `scripts/domains.json`; this file is at `scripts/data/domains.json`. scripts/data/ is where every other scripts-owned JSON already lives (20 of them), and the contract's own .json predicate keeps a file at a fixed path only when a tool discovers it there. Nothing discovers this one, so data/ is the consistent home. The contract text should be corrected rather than this file moved.

Driver contract section 5d says scripts/ holds 28 tracked non-TypeScript files. Measured 2026-09-06 at ac817a647: 164 .ts, 24 .json, 19 .sh, 7 .txt, 2 .py, 2 .md, 218 total, so 54 are not TypeScript. The 28 is 19+2+7 and silently excludes the .json and .md files, which this partition has to classify too.
